# Summary Report on Kenya’s Population Projections 

## Background 

## The 2019 Kenya Population and Housing Census was conducted in the midnight of 24th/25th August as the reference point. It was conducted under the provisions of the Constitution of Kenya, 2010 (Fourth Schedule Part 1, Item 11), the Statistics (Amendment) Act, 2019 and the Statistics (Census of Population) Order, 2018 - Legal Notice No. 205 and the Cabinet Memorandum of May 2017 on the implementation of the 2019 population and housing census process. The theme for the census was “Counting Our People for Sustainable Development and Devolution of Services ”. 

## Uses of Population Projections 

## There are four distinct areas in which population projections are a necessary input: 1. Distribution of resources - national and county planners all need, for various purposes, to have some idea of likely future changes in size, composition and distribution of the population in their respective areas. 2. Advocacy – especially where there is a negative impact of a particular phenomenon on population or vice versa. 3. Research - Researchers frequently use projections to try to answer questions that relate to future economic and social development. 

## 4. Monitoring and evaluation - population projections become an important input for programmes not only during target setting, but also for monitoring and evaluation, especially at impact level. 

## 5. Private sector – population projections are a critical input in driving production and consumption although use of such projections by the private sector remains minimal in Kenya. 

## Population Projections 

## Populations is expected to increase throughout the projection period. Six top counties expected to experience the highest percentage of population are Samburu, Tana River, Narok, Lamu, Wajir and Turkana. In terms of numbers, Nairobi City, Kiambu, Nakuru, Narok and Kakamega counties are expected to have the highest increase. The table below presents Population Projections by County from 2020 to 2045. Sectoral Population Projections 

Sectoral Population Projections include school-age population, labour force and households are included in this monograph. Sectoral projections are essential for planning processes. 

Kenya’s School-age Population 

School-age population projections corresponded to both the CBC and 8-4-4 educational systems. CBC: pre-school - population age 4-5 years; lower primary - population age 6-11 years; junior secondary - population age 12-14 years; and senior secondary - population age 15-17 years. The population for the 8-4-4 educational system: pre-school - population age 3-5 years; primary - population age 6-13 years; and secondary - population age 14-17 years. The projected school-age population at national level is depicted in Table below.
